title: Firefox profiles
whyItMatters: A Firefox profile holds history, bookmarks, cookies, saved logins and open sessions. The folder name alone shows how many separate browsing identities were used.
source: Mozilla Support, where Firefox stores user data (profile folder with prefs.js); Linux default profile root ~/.mozilla/firefox: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-firefox-stores-user-data
notes: prefs.js marks a real profile, so cache and Crash Reports folders are skipped. Firefox 147+ on a fresh install uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mozilla/firefox instead; upgraded installs keep ~/.mozilla/firefox. profiles.ini can point at profiles stored elsewhere, which this rule does not follow.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Firefox, export your bookmarks from the Library and your passwords from the logins settings, and keep both files off this computer.
cleanup.signOut: In Firefox, open the account menu and disconnect this browser from sync, so the account keeps the data and this computer stops using it.
steps: Uninstall Firefox from the App Center if you are removing the browser itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes every Firefox profile on this computer: history, bookmarks, saved logins, cookies and the files you downloaded through the browser.
cleanup.source: Mozilla Support, Profiles - Where Firefox stores your bookmarks, passwords and other user data: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-firefox-stores-user-data
